docs.title: Dropsome Docs
docs.text:
Dropsome Docs A handy way to share SOL with newbies.

Dropsome makes it easy to send SOL to someone who does not have a wallet yet. You create a drop, share a claim link, and the receiver claims it after installing a wallet and importing the temporary recovery phrase. If the drop is never claimed, the sender can always refund it.

Info

Want to chat with our docs? Download an LLM-friendly text file of the full Dropsome docs.

  • Drop — send SOL with a link

    Set the amount, generate a claim link, and send it privately.

  • Claim — receive SOL from a link

    Open the link, import the temporary recovery phrase, connect your wallet, and the claim happens automatically.

  • Refund — get your SOL back

    If a drop is unclaimed, the sender can refund it at any time.

docs.title: Claim — receive SOL from a link
docs.text: If someone sent you a Dropsome drop, you do not need a wallet first. Open the claim link, install a wallet, import the temporary recovery phrase, connect your wallet to the page, and the claim happens automatically.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• a phone or computer with internet
  • a Solana wallet app
  • the claim link you received

docs.title: 1. Open the claim link
docs.text: The page will show the drop amount and your recovery phrase.

docs.title: 2. Install a wallet
docs.text:
Use an official wallet app such as:

  • Phantom — phantom.app
  • Solflare — solflare.com
  • Backpack — backpack.app

Only download from the official links

Fake wallet apps do exist. Use the wallet provider's official site or app store listing.

docs.title: 3. Import the wallet with the recovery phrase
docs.text:
This is the most important step. The claim page gives you a recovery phrase. That phrase belongs to a temporary wallet made for this drop.

You must import that exact wallet. Do not create a new wallet.

  1. Open your wallet app
  2. Choose Import wallet or Recover wallet
  3. Enter the recovery phrase exactly as shown
  4. Finish setup in the wallet app

Why you should not create a new wallet

The funds are locked to one specific wallet address. If you create a new wallet instead of importing the temporary one, the drop will not be there.

After importing, connect the wallet on the claim page. The claim happens automatically once the correct wallet is connected — no button to click. The transaction usually completes in a few seconds.

docs.title: 5. Your SOL is now in your wallet
docs.text: Once confirmed, the SOL appears in the wallet you imported. You can hold it, send it, or move it to another wallet later.

docs.title: Recommended: move funds to your own wallet
docs.text:
The imported wallet was created for the drop. For best security, create a fresh wallet and move the funds there:

  1. Create a new wallet in your app and save its recovery phrase securely
  2. Send the claimed SOL from the temporary wallet to your new wallet address
  3. Delete the temporary wallet if you no longer need it

This keeps your long-term funds in a wallet you control and manage yourself.

docs.title: What is a recovery phrase?
docs.text:
A recovery phrase is a list of 12–24 words that acts like the master key to a wallet. Anyone who has it can control that wallet.

  • wallet apps use this standard format
  • the phrase on the claim page is the only way to access the drop wallet
  • never share it with anyone, even the sender

docs.title: Safety checklist
docs.text:
• Downloaded the wallet from the official app/site only
  • Imported the wallet using the recovery phrase from the claim page
  • Confirmed the SOL appeared in the wallet after automatic claim
  • Moved funds to a wallet you control long-term
  • Deleted or archived the claim link after claiming
  • Never shared the recovery phrase with anyone

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Likely cause Fix "Wallet not found" Wrong phrase entered or a new wallet was created instead of importing Re-import the exact recovery phrase from the claim page "Already claimed" Someone else used the link Contact the sender; they may still be able to refund if it is still unclaimed Network error / timeout Solana congestion or RPC issue Wait a minute and retry; check Solana status "Invalid recovery phrase" Typo, wrong order, or extra spaces Copy and paste the phrase carefully and use the exact order shown

docs.title: Drop — send SOL with a link
docs.text: A drop lets you send SOL without collecting a wallet address in advance. The app creates a temporary wallet, locks the funds in a program vault, and gives you a claim link to share privately.

docs.title: 1. Enter the amount
docs.text: Choose the amount of SOL you want to send. The app will generate a temporary wallet and a unique claim link.

docs.title: 2. Funds are locked on-chain
docs.text: The SOL, plus a little gas reserve and app fee, is stored in a Dropsome vault on Solana until the receiver claims it or you refund it.

docs.title: 3. Share the link privately
docs.text: Send the claim link through a private channel: text message, encrypted email, DM, or in person. Anyone who holds the link can claim the drop.

docs.title: What happens on-chain
docs.text:
When you create a drop, the app creates a vault and a record for that drop:

  • the vault holds the SOL until claim or refund
  • the record tracks the sender, temporary receiver wallet, amount, and claim state
  • the temporary wallet is the only wallet authorized to claim the funds
  • the sender can refund at any time while the drop remains unclaimed

This is not a generic airdrop flow. Each drop is tied to one sender and one temporary receiver wallet.

docs.title: Fees and balances
docs.text:
Fee Who pays Typical behavior Service fee Sender Small app fee charged by the protocol Network fee reserve Sender Set aside to cover the receiver’s claim transaction Rent exemption Sender Temporarily locked and returned on claim or refund

The app shows the total before you confirm. You need enough SOL to cover the drop amount plus fees.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• a Solana wallet such as Phantom, Solflare, or Backpack
  • enough SOL for the amount plus fees
  • an internet connection and a private way to send the claim link

docs.title: Security reminders
docs.text:
Treat the claim link like cash

Anyone who has the link can claim the funds. Share it only through a private, trusted channel.

Start small

If you are testing the flow for the first time, use a small amount.

Refund is always available

As long as the drop remains unclaimed, you can refund the full amount back to your wallet. See Refund.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Likely cause Fix "Insufficient balance" Not enough SOL for the amount and fees Add more SOL or lower the amount Transaction failed Network congestion or RPC issue Retry in a minute and check Solana status Drop not showing in refund flow Wrong wallet connected or already claimed Connect the original sender wallet and check the claim status

docs.title: Refund — get your SOL back
docs.text: If a drop is still unclaimed, the original sender can refund it at any time. The funds stay in the vault until someone claims them or the sender chooses to return them.

docs.title: When you can refund
docs.text:
• the drop is still unclaimed
  • you connect the same wallet that created the drop
  • the drop is still tied to the original sender and receiver wallet

There is no automatic expiry in the basic refund flow.

docs.title: 1. Connect the sender wallet
docs.text: Open the refund page and connect the wallet that created the drop.

docs.title: 2. Review your unclaimed drops
docs.text: You will see the active drops associated with that wallet, including the amount and status.

docs.title: 3. Select a drop and click Refund
docs.text: Choose the drop or drops you want to return and sign the transaction.

docs.title: 4. Confirm the transaction
docs.text: The funds return to your wallet once the transaction is confirmed. The claim link becomes invalid after refund.

docs.title: On-chain mechanics
docs.text:
When you refund:

  • the program closes the associated record
  • the vault is emptied and returned to the sender wallet
  • the temporary receiver wallet is no longer authorized to claim
  • the original sender keeps control of the funds while the drop is active

This keeps the refund flow simple and predictable: if it was never claimed, the sender can always recover it.

docs.title: Important notes
docs.text:
No partial refund

You refund the whole drop, not a portion of it.

Only the sender can refund

The refund transaction must be signed by the wallet that originally created the drop.

Refund right away if the link was shared carelessly

If a claim link was posted publicly or sent to the wrong person, refund it immediately to stop the drop from being claimed.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Likely cause Fix Drop not showing Wrong wallet connected or already claimed Connect the original sender wallet and check the claim status Transaction failed RPC issue or network congestion Retry in a minute and check Solana status "Already claimed" Someone used the claim link before the refund The funds were transferred out; if this was unexpected, contact the recipient

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Dropsome, accessible at https://dropsome.xyz, values the privacy of participants who visit and interact with the interface (the “Interface”). We are committed to minimizing the collection of personal data and ensuring transparency about any data processing activities.

This Privacy Policy outlines the types of data that may be processed when using the Interface and the third-party services involved in its operation.

docs.title: 2. Data We Do Not Collect
docs.text:
• The Dropsome does not collect, store, or process personally identifiable information (PII), such as names, emails, or IP addresses.
  • We do not use cookies, trackers, or store user data on external databases.
  • The Dropsome operates as a non-custodial application, meaning all transactions occur directly on the blockchain.

docs.title: 3. Third-Party Services
docs.text:
To operate effectively, the Interface relies on third-party service providers. These providers may process certain technical data to ensure platform stability, performance, and security. The categories of third-party services include:

  • Technical Infrastructure Providers – Hosting, security, and networking services that enable the Interface to function.
  • Development & Monitoring Tools – Services used for debugging and maintaining platform stability.
  • Communication Vendors – Platforms facilitating support inquiries.
  • Analytics & Performance Vendors – Tools that may collect anonymized data to improve usability and security.

docs.title: 4. Data Processed in Connection with the Interface
Types of Data Processed
docs.text:
To the maximum extent possible, Dropsome minimizes data collection. However, interacting with the Interface may involve the following types of data processing:

  1. Blockchain Data
  2. Wallet addresses (public blockchain addresses), transactions, and balance information are publicly accessible on the blockchain.
  3. The Interface does not store or process this data off-chain.
  4. Public blockchain addresses may be used to analyze user journeys in an aggregated and anonymized manner to improve the user experience.

  5. Dropsome does not track or process blockchain data at an individual user level.

  6. Technical and Security Data

  7. Third-party service providers (e.g., hosting and security vendors) may process certain technical data such as IP addresses, device/browser details, and traffic patterns as part of maintaining platform integrity.

  8. These logs are typically stored by third-party service providers and are not used by Dropsome for tracking or profiling users.

  9. Log Files

  10. The Interface follows standard logging practices, which may include network logs for security, debugging, and performance monitoring.
  11. This data is processed in an aggregated and anonymized manner where possible.
  12. Dropsome does not link log file data to personally identifiable information.

docs.title: How and Why We Use This Data
docs.text:
• Security & Fraud Prevention – Ensuring platform integrity and identifying irregular activity.
  • Performance & Optimization – Improving the Interface by analyzing anonymized usage trends.
  • Technical Support – Debugging issues and maintaining reliability.

Dropsome does not use this data for advertising, tracking, or selling to third parties.

docs.title: 5. Data Retention
docs.text:
• Dropsome does not store any user data off-chain.
  • Any logs collected by third-party services follow their respective retention policies.
  • Aggregated data, which cannot directly identify a user, may be retained for service improvement purposes.

docs.title: 6. Security & User Responsibility
docs.text:
• The Interface encrypts the secret phrase before sharing it with the receiver.
  • We never request private keys or seed phrases. Users should never enter these into any third-party websites.
  • Users remain fully responsible for safeguarding their wallet credentials.

docs.title: 7. User Rights & Contact
docs.text: Since the Interface does not collect personal data, users do not need to request access, modification, or deletion of any stored information. For general inquiries, please contact us at legal@dropsome.xyz.

docs.title: 8. Changes to This Policy
docs.text: We may update this policy as needed. The latest version will always be available at https://dropsome.xyz. Continued use of the Interface constitutes acceptance of the updated Privacy Policy.

docs.title: Disclaimer & safety notes
docs.text:
Dropsome was created to simplify small cryptocurrency transfers such as loans and gifts, not for storing large amounts. This page explains, in plain language, what using a “magic link” and a generated wallet means for your security, and how to use Dropsome in a safer way.

You use Dropsome at your own risk.

docs.title: How the magic link works
docs.text:
When you create a drop, Dropsome generates a new wallet for that drop. The secret phrase (seed phrase) for this wallet is:

  • Generated on our backend.
  • Encrypted with a server-side key.
  • Embedded (in encrypted form) in the claim link you share.

When the receiver opens the claim link in the official Dropsome app:

  • The page automatically sends the encrypted data to our server.
  • The server decrypts the seed phrase and returns it to the page.
  • The receiver can then import that wallet into a Solana wallet app (for example Phantom, Solflare or Backpack).

The main risk is simple: if the link or the seed phrase is ever leaked or shared with the wrong person, they can claim or move the funds from that wallet.

docs.title: What this means for trust
docs.text:
• The sender and the receiver both have (or can get) access to the same seed phrase.
  • Either of them could keep a copy of it.
  • Anyone who sees that seed phrase later can restore the wallet and control whatever is still inside it.

Because of that, the drop wallet should be treated as temporary and shared‑risk, not as a long‑term personal wallet.

docs.title: Tips for senders
docs.text:
• Keep drops small. Use Dropsome for onboarding‑size gifts, not life savings.

  • Share links in private. Send the claim link only to the intended person, preferably over a private, end‑to‑end encrypted channel (for example Signal, Telegram, WhatsApp, iMessage).

  • Delete the link when you’re done. After the drop is successfully claimed or refunded, remove the claim link from chats, notes, and other places where it was stored, and (if possible) ask the receiver to delete it on their side too.

  • Avoid copying the seed phrase. Don’t store it in notes, screenshots, email, cloud drives, or chats.

  • Use the refund option if something feels off. If you think the link was posted publicly or shared with the wrong person, and the drop is still unclaimed, use the refund flow to pull the funds back to your own wallet.

docs.title: Tips for receivers
docs.text:
• Treat the drop wallet as a one‑time wallet. Use it only to receive the gift from Dropsome and start diving into the world of cryptocurrency.

  • Move funds to your own wallet quickly. After you claim:

  • Figure out how to manage wallets on your own.
  • Create a new Solana wallet where only you know the seed phrase.
  • Transfer all SOL (and any tokens) from the drop wallet to your new wallet.

  • Stop using the drop wallet afterwards.

  • Do not use the drop wallet for savings. During claiming, the seed phrase or the link to it can easily travel through copy‑paste, messengers, screenshots, or shared devices. Because of that, it’s safest to treat this wallet as short‑term only and not keep savings there.

  • Only enter the seed phrase in trusted wallet apps. Install wallet apps from their official websites or app stores, and never type the seed phrase into random websites, bots, or forms.

docs.title: General security reminders
docs.text:
• Keep any seed phrase you care about offline and stored safely.
  • Always double‑check that you are on the real Dropsome site before creating or claiming a drop.
  • Be suspicious of anyone asking you to send them your seed phrase or a screenshot of it — no one legitimate needs it.

Using Dropsome, like any on-chain tool, involves risk. Please make sure you understand these points before you create or claim a drop.

docs.title: 2. Description of Service
docs.text:
Dropsome is a decentralized finance (DeFi) application built on the Solana blockchain, designed to facilitate the sharing of small amounts of SOL with individuals who do not yet have a wallet. The Interface enables the following features: * Drop: Users ("Depositors") can send SOL to a Program-Derived Address (PDA) account, which creates a new encrypted wallet for the recipient. The wallet data is encrypted and shared via a link. When the link is opened, the recipient receives clear instructions to set up and initialize the wallet. * Claim: Upon opening the link and initializing the wallet, a transaction transfers the deposited SOL from the PDA to the recipient's new wallet. * Refund: Depositors can reclaim unclaimed deposits if the recipient does not claim the SOL.

The application (Interface) consists of an on-chain Solana program and a web interface.

docs.title: Encryption — how the claim link works
docs.text: Dropsome uses an encrypted claim link to deliver a temporary wallet's recovery phrase to the receiver. The recovery phrase is generated on demand, encrypted in the app backend, and decrypted when the receiver opens the link.

docs.title: The short version
docs.text:
1. The backend generates a temporary wallet for the drop
  2. The recovery phrase is encrypted with a server-side key
  3. The ciphertext is embedded in the claim URL as a data payload
  4. The receiver opens the claim page and requests decryption from the API
  5. The app returns the recovery phrase so the user can import it into a wallet

This keeps the flow simple for new users while preserving the on-chain authorization model.

docs.title: Threat model
docs.text:
What is protected How Recovery phrase in the claim link The link contains encrypted ciphertext, not the phrase in plain text Recovery phrase in the Dropsome backend Not persisted by the claim endpoint; decrypted only on demand Recovery phrase in the browser Returned to the claiming browser so the user can import the wallet Server key compromise Could enable decryption of unclaimed drop payloads

Trust assumption

The server holds the decryption key and the claim flow returns the decrypted recovery phrase to the receiver's browser. Dropsome does not persist the phrase in the backend, but the claim payload is a bearer credential: anyone who obtains the claim link or its encrypted data value may be able to claim the drop. Use this flow for small amounts and share links privately.

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
• Algorithm: AES-256-CBC
  • Key: A server-side key kept in environment configuration
  • IV: Random per encryption so the same recovery phrase does not produce the same ciphertext
  • Output: encrypted payload is encoded and embedded in the claim URL

AES-256-CBC provides confidentiality for the payload, but it is not an authenticated-encryption mode. The claim endpoint must therefore be treated as part of the trusted application flow; this documentation is not a claim that the payload is tamper-proof.

docs.title: Link format
docs.text:
https://dropsome.xyz/claim?data=<encrypted_payload>

The encrypted payload: - is embedded in the URL as data, not shown to the user in plain text - is sent to the API for decryption over HTTPS when the receiver opens the link - may be retained in browser history, copied messages, analytics, referrer data, or infrastructure access logs that record full URLs - is not intended to be used as a public identifier or shared outside the intended claim flow

The current implementation uses a query parameter rather than a URL fragment. Dropsome's own claim endpoint does not persist the payload or log the decrypted phrase, but the app cannot guarantee that every browser, hosting provider, proxy, monitoring service, or messaging platform will omit the URL from its own records.

docs.title: Decryption flow
docs.text:
1. The receiver opens the claim link
  2. The frontend reads the encrypted payload from the URL
  3. The frontend sends it to the API for decryption
  4. The server decrypts it and returns the recovery phrase to the browser
  5. The receiver imports the phrase into a wallet app

The phrase is not stored in local storage or cookies by the app.

docs.title: As a sender
docs.text:
• the claim link is the secret used to retrieve the drop
  • share it only through a trusted private channel
  • keep the link out of public, shared, or automatically indexed spaces
  • if the link is exposed and the drop is still unclaimed, use the refund flow immediately

docs.title: As a receiver
docs.text:
• the recovery phrase shown on the claim page is the only copy needed to access the drop wallet
  • import it into a wallet immediately
  • move the funds to a wallet you control after claiming
  • avoid opening claim links on shared devices or in browsers with untrusted extensions

docs.title: If you are building on Dropsome
docs.text:
• keep the decryption key in a secure environment variable
  • protect the decryption endpoint with the same rate limiting and authentication model as the rest of the app
  • treat the server as a trusted component for the claim flow

docs.title: Solana Program — on-chain mechanics
docs.text: The Dropsome program handles the escrow, claim, and refund logic for each drop. This page summarizes the core account model and transaction flow used by the app.

docs.title: Program ID
docs.text: Mainnet: DSdHwC1vGPL4KzNAhgxMYggZnBBaY8upKx6uo655kVYZ

docs.title: AppState (global config)
docs.text:
A single PDA at ["app_state"] stores global config for the app.

pub struct AppState {
    pub is_initialized: bool,
    pub authority: Pubkey,
    pub is_active: bool,
    pub network_fee_reserve: u64,
    pub treasury: Pubkey,
    pub fee_basis_points: u16,
    pub min_drop_amount: u64,
}

docs.title: Record (per drop)
docs.text:
A PDA at ["record", sender, receiver] tracks each active drop.

pub struct Record {
    pub sender: Pubkey,
    pub receiver: Pubkey,
    pub vault: Pubkey,
    pub amount: u64,
}

docs.title: Vault (per drop)
docs.text: A PDA at ["vault", sender, receiver] holds the SOL while the drop is active.

docs.title: 1. drop — create a drop
docs.text:
Accounts: sender, temporary receiver keypair, vault, record, app state, treasury, system program

Flow: 1. validate the amount against the minimum and app state 2. calculate the service fee and reserve requirements 3. initialize the Record account with sender, receiver, vault, and amount 4. transfer the network fee reserve to the receiver wallet 5. transfer the drop amount and rent exemption into the vault 6. transfer the service fee to the treasury

The receiver is a freshly generated wallet keypair, not a PDA. The frontend provides its public key to the program as the claim target.

docs.title: 2. claim — receiver claims funds
docs.text:
Accounts: claimer signer, vault, record, system program

Flow: 1. verify the signer matches the record.receiver 2. transfer the vault balance to the receiver wallet 3. close the Record account so rent goes back to the sender 4. let the runtime close the empty vault account

Only the wallet generated for the drop can claim it.

docs.title: 3. refund — sender reclaims unclaimed funds
docs.text:
Accounts: sender signer, vault, record, system program

Flow: 1. verify the signer matches the original record.sender 2. transfer the vault balance back to the sender wallet 3. close the Record account

Only the original sender can refund. There is no third-party refund path.

docs.title: 4. update — admin config update
docs.text:
Accounts: authority signer, app state

This updates the global state such as fee settings, min amount, active status, and treasury destination.

docs.title: Fees
docs.text:
Fee Paid by Destination Typical behavior Service fee Sender Treasury Small app fee Network fee reserve Sender Receiver wallet Covers claim transaction gas Vault rent exemption Sender Returned on claim/refund Temporarily locked in the vault

The UI should show the total before confirmation so the sender sees the full cost.

docs.title: Security properties
docs.text:
• single claimer — only the generated temporary wallet can claim
  • single refunder — only the original sender can refund
  • no partial refunds — each drop is refunded in full or not at all
  • rent is returned — the accounts are closed cleanly on claim or refund
  • funds stay in escrow until a valid claim or refund occurs

docs.title: Frontend integration
docs.text: Action Frontend behavior Program call Drop generates receiver keypair, encrypts recovery phrase, builds link drop Claim decrypts recovery phrase, user imports wallet, connects it claim Refund lists sender-owned unclaimed records and builds tx refund

docs.title: Deploy and upgrade
docs.text:
• Framework: Anchor (Rust)
  • Program authority: app state authority
  • IDL: generated at build and used by the frontend for transaction construction
